sources.title: Exact tagged repository question and frozen Batch 0033 source boundary
Longest Consecutive deterministic JDK 21 validation against independent sorting oracle

claims.text: The repository source identifies Longest Consecutive Sequence (LeetCode 128); Java/null/mutation/integer-bound details are answer-side contracts.
Under the explicit candidate contract, the exact fenced Java uses a HashSet, starts only at values without representable predecessors, and guards Java int boundary arithmetic.
The JDK 21 fixture passes six named cases, null rejection, non-mutation, both int-boundary directions, and all 97,656 bounded arrays against an independent sorting oracle.

boundary_tests.expected: all arrays length 0..7 over {-2,-1,0,1,2} match sorting oracle

findings: The preserved repository source identifies the task as Longest Consecutive Sequence (LeetCode 128) and does not preserve a Java signature, null behavior, mutation policy, exact integer bounds, or a mandatory data structure in the repository snapshot.
The candidate explicitly labels int[] input, empty=0, null rejection, non-mutation and the HashSet implementation as answer-side executable contracts rather than recovered source facts.
The displayed Java is byte-for-byte identical to the validated fixture, compiles under JDK 21, de-duplicates values, and expands a consecutive run only from a value with no representable predecessor.
The Integer.MIN_VALUE and Integer.MAX_VALUE guards prevent Java int wraparound from incorrectly connecting the two numeric extremes; fixed tests cover both boundary directions.

An independent sorting oracle checks all 97,656 arrays of lengths 0 through 7 over {-2,-1,0,1,2}, while named cases cover classic examples, duplicates, all-equal input, null rejection and non-mutation.

The average O(n) claim is bounded to the average constant-time HashSet membership assumption; the answer also presents sorting as an O(n log n) alternative and does not claim strict worst-case linear hashing.
No fabricated project experience, placeholder code, unrelated topic content, uncovered source variant, or material unsupported claim remains.
